name: py-ledger
description: A Python household ledger on sqlite3, from an empty directory. Rules: amounts as integer cents (u2), only the standard library (u5), type hints on every function (u9, lifted at u19). Values reused later: the schema version (u6, u16), commit hashes (u8, u15, u23), the March total (u12, u21).
turns: Let's write a small household ledger in Python 3 in this empty directory. Start with git init, a ledger/ package, and ledger/db.py that opens a sqlite3 database and creates a transactions table with id, date, description, category and amount. Add tests under tests/ that run with python3 -m unittest, and run them.
Always store amounts as integer cents, never as floats. Parse user input like 12.34 into 1234 with exact decimal handling.
Add ledger/cli.py with an add command: python3 -m ledger.cli add 2026-03-04 "Groceries" food 54.20. Test it end to end with a temporary database file.
Add a list command that prints transactions for a month, newest first, with amounts formatted back to two decimals.
Use only the Python standard library in this project: no pip packages, not even for tests.
Add a schema_version table and set the version to 1. Write the migration code so that opening an older database upgrades it. Tell me the version number you stored.
Generate a sample data file, fixtures/march.csv, with about 40 transactions across food, rent, transport and fun for March 2026, and add an import command that loads it.
Commit everything so far with a short message and tell me the hash.
Every function must have type hints, parameters and return values both. Go through the existing code and add any that are missing.
Add a report command that prints the total per category for a month and a grand total at the bottom.
Make the report command handle a month with no transactions by printing a short message in place of an empty table, and add a test.
Import the March fixture into a fresh database and run the report for March 2026. What is the grand total?
Add a budget table (category, monthly limit in cents) and a set-budget command. The report should show the remaining budget next to each category.
Bump the schema to version 2 for the budget table, with a migration from version 1, and a test that opens a version 1 database and checks it was upgraded.
Commit this and give me the hash.
Which schema version did we start with, and what did the first migration add?
Add an export command that writes a month's transactions to CSV with the standard csv module, and a round-trip test with import.
The import command should skip rows it has already imported. Use a hash of date, description and amount to detect duplicates, and test it by importing the March fixture twice.
The type hint rule is lifted for test files; keep it for the ledger package itself.
Add a --json flag to the report command that prints the same numbers as a JSON object.
Run the March report again after the duplicate-import fix. Does the grand total still match the number you gave me earlier?
Write a README.md with the commands and one example each.
Run the full test suite, commit with a message listing the commands, and give me the hash.
Show me git log --oneline and tell me which commit introduced the budget table.
Final pass: list the rules I gave you during this session and check the code against each one.
